| **Where it lives** | New crate `nmp-nip-ad`, sibling to `nmp-nip05` (one-crate-per-NIP convention). Extract the shared bounded-GET + SSRF `host_guard` into a common crate both depend on — don't fork security-critical code. | [...] The rest of the design skeleton both comments agreed on stands: new `nmp-nip-ad` crate, shared SSRF-guarded http crate (absorbing both the nip05 *and* nip57 duplicate GETs), new `AdUrlState::ResolutionFailed` fail-open state, and reuse of the existing `nevent`/`naddr` relay-hint seam. [...] (3) Crates — ADDED: nmp-wellknown-http (shared SSRF guard + bounded http_get_json, killed the forked copies in nip05 AND nip57), nmp-nip-ad (parse/http/policy/ui_codes/ownership + live test). MODIFIED: nmp-nip05 & nmp-nip57 (migrated onto shared crate, local copies deleted), nmp-core (InputIntentTarget::AdCandidate), nmp-intent (rung 4.5 + recognizer + tests), nmp-native-runtime (dispatch arm), workspace Cargo.toml + release/nmp-release.toml.

(4) DEFERRED (precise spec in PR body): the whole moment-1/moment-2 DELIVERY hinges on a kernel primitive that does not exist — opening an arbitrary nostr::Filter against one-shot site relays (InterestShape::relay_pin) into a 0..N-event view. Your override ("keep the full filter, no single-pointer reduction") rules out the only existing seam (refs RefShape::Event). NIP-50 open_search can't carry a plain filter (it forces an FTS query); DynamicTargetProjection is target-based + private. So: ResolveAdCommand + that collection primitive, then Layer B (Segment/WireNode AdCandidateUrl = a full FlatBuffers+Swift+Kotlin+~188-renderer-site wire change, pure churn until the resolver exists) are the follow-up, blocked on primitive #1. Recommend a fast-follow issue for the collection primitive.

(5) Deviations: no EmbedTarget reduction (per your override — full nostr::Filter kept); shared http_get_json is redirects(0) so nip57 no longer follows redirects (security hardening, 147 tests still green); WebOfTrust/FollowsOnly are closure-generic to avoid an nmp-wot dep. [...] - **`nmp-wellknown-http`** — shared SSRF guard + bounded GET, which killed the **duplicated** `http_get_json` in *both* nip05 and nip57 (that consolidation was overdue independent of this feature). [...] 1) RULE E (real bug, FIXED): classified nmp-wellknown-http at L1 in the Rule E crate-layer map (rule_e.rs) — it's a network-transport util depended on only by the L4 protocol crates, so L1 sits below them with no upward edge. nmp-nip-ad was already covered by the nmp-nip* → L4 fallback, so only wellknown-http needed adding.
